procedural_matters: The race committee was represented by Andre Boronat (race committee member on the pin-end finish vessel).
FRA 276 was represented by Quentin Maydieu.
FRA 1480 was represented by Nicolas Salet.
The race committee provided video evidence.
Basile Buisson (spi trimmer of FRA 432) gave evidence as a witness for FRA 276.
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
Hearing No. 11 was heard together with hearing No. 6 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since both hearings arose from the same incident.
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 4-5 knots of wind and flat sea.
FRA 276 and FRA 1480 were both approaching the finish line on starboard tack.
When entering the zone of the pin-end finish vessel, the bowsprit of FRA 276 was overlapped inside of FRA 1480.
Both boats bore away to the finish line, the overlap was broken, and FRA 1480 became clear ahead.
There was contact between the bowsprit of FRA 276 and the stern of FRA 1480.
There was contact between the bow of FRA 276 and the bow of the pin-end finish vessel.
There was no damage to either boat.
conclusions: FRA 1480 outside overlapped at the zone failed to give FRA 276 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
FRA 1480's obligation to give FRA 276 mark-room did not change when the overlap was broken, as provided in the last sentence of RRS 18.2(a).
FRA 1480 caused contact between FRA 276 and the pin-end finish vessel even though it was reasonably possible to avoid causing it, and broke RRS 14(c).
FRA 1480 did not avoid contact with FRA 276 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

It was not reasonably possible for FRA 276 the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with FRA 1480 when it became clear that FRA 1480 was not giving mark-room. FRA 276 did not break RRS 14(a).
FRA 276 clear astern failed to keep clear of FRA 1480 clear ahead, and broke RRS 12.
FRA 276 touched the pin-end finish vessel and broke RRS 31.
Since FRA 276 broke RRS 12 and 31 while she was sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for these breaches.
